rv.q: In these moments there is a higher power being channelled, and it’s pure joy to witness it.
It’s the two sensational performances that make the evening.
Over a dozen songs are delivered with a mix of spirituality and pure, uplifting, power and energy.
The combination is dynamite, and makes for an evening fit to honour the memory of two trailblazing women.
Being as constricted as it is to one setting, and one point in time, inevitably sometimes Marie & Rosetta runs out of steam.
Ultimately, Marie and Rosetta is a production elevated by extraordinary musical talent but held back by a script that never quite matches its subject’s legacy.

Brant’s story, though, never lives up to these performances, a list of biographical knowledge woven into the dialogue without truly getting beneath the surface of either woman, their hard-won self-belief or the supportive warmth that brought them together.
The two performances are electric, and it is simply a joy to see two artistes at the top of their game in a fitting tribute to forgotten pioneers.
Often hitting all of the right notes, Marie & Rosetta raises the roof at @SohoPlace, making for an uplifting performance that will fill your heart with music.
It’s entertaining and filled with impressive performances, yet the story never quite reaches the emotional depth it promises.
With certain reservations, so did I, but the luminous performances by Beverley Knight and Ntombizodwa Ndlovu alone are well worth the price of admission.

cn.t: Beverley Knight delivers a powerhouse performance that elevates George Brant's modest two-hander about gospel pioneer Sister Rosetta Tharpe. Critics praise the vocals and music while finding the script somewhat thin and overly familiar.
